title: The Day Niagara Falls Went Silent
topic: The day Niagara Falls went silent (1848)
format_note: User-specified ~35 s historical Short with a user-given first line ('Niagara Falls once went silent.'), so it overrides the 50-60 s / 180-210 word targets and the He/It's/You opener on purpose (106 words, 32.6 s). The river and falls are drawn far narrower than real so both banks read in a 9:16 frame; the musket is drawn about 1.5x its size so it reads on a phone.
mechanism: Gale winds drove Lake Erie's broken ice fields into the mouth of the Niagara River, where the floes jammed into a dam like a cork in a bottle; with no water coming in, the river below drained and the falls stopped for about thirty hours until the wind shifted and the dam broke.

beats.hook: Roaring Horseshoe Falls thunders at the lens, mist and rainbow; HARD CUT to the same view in dead silence: bare wet rock, a trickle; the miller's face in the moonlight
beats.story: A village miller and his family by the Niagara River on the night of 29 March 1848; his water wheel creaks to a stop
beats.rise: Out on the riverbed at dawn people stroll, laugh, a rider trots across, a boy finds a musket: the river is theirs
beats.twist: Event: the wind turns, the ice dam at Lake Erie cracks apart and a wall of water comes down the channel at the people on the bed
beats.mechanism: Labelled physical props: LAKE ERIE fingerpost where the gale shoves the ice sheets, a giant cork-shaped ice jam at the river mouth beside a NIAGARA RIVER post, the miller's stopped water wheel, a pocket watch counting the hours
beats.ending: The roaring falls with a rainbow, the family cheering on the bank; the camera rushes back to the opening view of the falls (loop)
